responses_to_findings.finding: BLOCKING: selfcheck_v2.py D_numerical_rank<=rank(=6) assertion spuriously fails because the FP32-generated ill-conditioned xh has numerical rank 12 (6 rounding modes at ~3-4e-8 relative amplified by s/rho into D singular values ~0.026-0.12 >> 1e-6*smax); runner aborts at selfcheck before any site, wasting the single authorized job.
responses_to_findings.fix_option_chosen: (a) reviewer-preferred: construct the ill-conditioned X in F64 so numerical rank == mathematical rank 6
responses_to_findings.detail: selfcheck_v2.py L79-86: xh = torch.randn(nh,rank,device=dev,dtype=torch.float64) @ torch.randn(rank,dh,device=dev,dtype=torch.float64); xsh=[xh,xh.clone()]; residuals formed in F64 from this X: rsh=[y.double() - xh @ a_h.double() for y in ysh]. The stable solve receives the F64 xsh/rsh; its F64 null modes (~1e-14 absolute, ~1e-16 relative) contribute ~s/rho ~ 1e-9 absolute to D singular values, ~5 orders below the 1e-6*smax threshold (~1e-5), so D_numerical_rank=6 and the RETAINED assertion (L118-119) is now a valid certificate rather than a spurious abort. The ORIGINAL FP32 path is fed FP32-ROUNDED COPIES: free_ridge_fit_fp32_original([x.float() for x in xsh], ysh, [r.float() for r in rsh], gh, nsh, a_h, lam_h) (L122-123), mirroring R1's FP32 data path exactly, so its FP32 Gram/RHS formation still injects ~1e-7 relative null-space noise amplified by g^2/rho ~ 1e6-1e7; the leak discrimination is preserved. The oos_old threshold was simultaneously aligned from 1e-6 to the pre-registered 1e-4 (L131-132, scope.json ridge.certificates), and oos_old is measured against bases_h['calgram'] (R1's exact Gram criterion). WHY option (a): it keeps the exact mathematical rank bound as a real executed certificate (stronger than deleting the assertion or loosening the bound to the numerical row rank), keeps the test in the true rank-deficient regime the real sites face, and preserves the FP32-leak discrimination by construction instead of relying on the rounding artifact of the test generator itself.

responses_to_findings.finding: OBSERVATION: icc_two_residual_decomposed decomposition_rel_residual<=1e-10 could theoretically trip from F64 rounding under near-perfect A~-B cancellation.
responses_to_findings.detail: Acknowledged. The identity is algebraically exact in F64 and the residual is normalized by max(total_f64,1e-30); at the frozen svd_r512 two-residual config the propagated stage-1 and stage-2 terms are not expected to cancel to that degree, and the zero-factor control is exact by construction. If a real source ever trips it the job fails loudly (no silent corruption), and per the failure plan the job is diagnosed and re-reviewed as a new scope, never silently resubmitted. No pre-execution change.
